title: Academy scorer: training review
system: MeridianX Academy offline scorers (ml/), seven edges, train pool only
verdict: No scorer passes: all 20 (the reference and the four pre-registered challenger configurations) are rejected challengers; none is promoted. The best kept-minus-skipped t out of fold is 0.95 (nq-open · mono-gbt, n 206); the smallest Holm-corrected p of a scorer's own test is 1.0. Three edges are too small to support a trained scorer.
examReadsNote: the review and the trainer read the train pool only; the loader drops 733 rows of other pools unread

configs.gbt: C0, the reference: gradient-boosted trees (depth 2, 120 trees) on 70 inputs
configs.logit-short: C1: logistic regression, L2 (C 0.1), the 7 short-list inputs
configs.mono-gbt: C2: boosted stumps (depth 1, 60 trees) on the short list, non-decreasing in the policy's five factors
configs.pooled-logit: C3: one logistic regression (C 0.1) over all seven edges, the short list plus one intercept per edge
configs.ridge-netR: C4: ridge regression of net R (alpha 100), the short list; its output is an expected R, never a probability

family.note: a test with two or three skipped trades can show a large Welch t when those few trades happen to have nearly the same result (two full stops): the permutation p beside it is the honest reading. No such test is a scorer's own verdict test

sources.geometry: the candidate's entry, stop and target (fixed by the rule at t) against bars that had closed at t
sources.side: the candidate's side against bars that had closed at t
sources.bars: bars that had closed at t (MXR.snapshot keeps a bar only when bar.time + tfSec <= t)
sources.edge: the id of the edge that fired (pooled scorers only)

features.how: traced in assets/academy-core.js build(): every value is computed from snapshot.bars (closed bars only), snapshot.t and the candidate's side / entry / stop / target; outcomes are joined to the matrix afterwards as label columns

marketEntryNote.what: the entry of a market order is the price it is filled at. For gmp that is the open of the first M1 bar after t, one tick after the decision time; the features that use the entry (rr, stopAtr, targetAtr, entryOffset, geomOk, entryLoc, entryZone, locFor, oppLiq, oppLiqFrac) carry that tick

features.driftLine: |standardised mean difference| of at least 0.25 between the first and the second half (by time) of a scope's usable train rows

labels.label: win = 1 when the position's net R (after the round-trip cost) is above 0, else 0; the ridge configuration fits net R itself
labels.position: net R is the whole position as the study books it: the first unit plus its pyramid add (replica, mosha-bo, gtrend), with the rule's size where the rule sizes
labels.unfilled: an order that never filled (missed, expired, cancelled) has no label and is in no training row, no metric and no average
labels.timeExits: a time exit is labelled like any other exit: by the sign of its net R
labels.afterTheExit: the recorded exit time is the first unit's. An add leg is managed on its own and can close later, up to the first unit's deadline, so the label of a position with an add can depend on prices after the recorded exit
labels.independence: trades of one edge that are open together share the same market move: a Welch t treats them as independent, so it overstates the evidence where openedWhileAnotherWasOpenShare is high
labels.classBalance: win rates run from 0.24 (replica) to 0.51 (gtl). No class weights are used: the AUC and the kept-minus-skipped test do not depend on the balance, and probabilities are judged against the prior rate
labels.selection: training on filled orders only conditions on something not known at the signal time for the two limit-order edges (mosha-bo, geg): the scorer then estimates P(win | the order fills)

permutation.what: win and net R shuffled together inside each edge, every scorer re-run walk-forward

canary.what: scratch runs with one leaking column added: canaryNetR = the trade's net R plus unit normal noise; canaryHoldHours = hours from the signal to the exit

foldBoundaries.what: counted at every test-block start of the design, summed over the blocks of a scope. firstUnitOpen = the recorded exit is after the block's start. addMayBeOpen / labelMayBeOpen = the position's last possible close (an add leg's deadline plus a weekend) is after it. oldRule = the first trainer's rule (first-unit exit plus one day). newRule = signal time plus the edge's label window

scramble.what: every label column and every feature value of every row outside the train pool replaced with noise, then python ml/train.py run on both matrices

power.what: mde = the smallest kept-minus-skipped difference in net R a trade that gives a Welch t of 2 when both groups have the edge's own SD: 2 x SD x sqrt(1/kept + 1/skipped). eventsPerInput = trades of the smaller class divided by the number of inputs
power.line: an edge with fewer than 10 events per input even for the 7-input configurations, on all of its trades, cannot support a trained scorer
power.noteOnTheFitted: for the four fitted edges the first training window holds 2 to 15 events per input with 7 inputs and under 2 with 70: the 70-input reference is fitted far beyond what the data supports

mosha-bo.mdeOn: all of its usable trades, as if none were needed for fitting (it has no out-of-fold sample)

gtrend.mdeOn: all of its usable trades, as if none were needed for fitting (it has no out-of-fold sample)

geg.mdeOn: all of its usable trades, as if none were needed for fitting (it has no out-of-fold sample)

seeds.what: the reference scorer (the only configuration that samples rows and columns), seeds [1, 7, 13, 29, 101]

calibration.what: out of fold, the scorer's own probability (before any Platt step). brierMinusPrior below 0 is better than the prior rate; the interval is a bootstrap over trades (2,000 resamples)
calibration.rule: no number may be shown as a probability unless it is calibrated out of fold; a scorer whose Brier interval does not sit below 0 has shown no probability skill

regimes.what: out of fold, kept against skipped inside each calendar year, each regimeBase label and each volState; and the overall t with one year left out at a time. Pooled scorers on edge-adjusted net R. A t is given only when both groups have at least 5 trades

protocol.what: the reference scorer (C0) walked forward four ways. The fitted trees are the same in all four: only which rows train a fold and which trades choose a threshold change

policyFactors.what: the stored fits of the short-list configurations, on every usable train row: which inputs the constrained stumps split on, and the sign of each policy factor's weight in the logistic fits. In sample: a description, not a test

deviations: Embargo: the pre-registration set the label window to the larger of the rule's bound and the longest observed signal-to-exit time. The run adds 72 hours (a weekend) to it, because a time exit that falls in the weekend is filled at the reopen. It is stricter, never looser.
Family size: the pre-registration lists the tests that make the Holm family; it gave no count. The run has 42.

Additions the pre-registration did not list, none of which a verdict depends on: a permutation p beside every family test with t >= 2; the per-edge prior rate as the Brier bar of the pooled scorers in the calibration table; a minimum of 5 trades a side for a t inside a year or a regime; the in-sample description of which short-list inputs the stored fits lean on; the reference scorer walked forward under the first trainer's rules, to measure what the two fixes changed.
